column4: The source-section root ع ل م is explained as a distinguishing sign; this verse names عَلَامَات, landmarks by which a traveler can identify the way.
The source-section dictionary form أَعْلَام means standards or mountains; here sailing ships themselves are signs and rise like الأعلام.
The source-section dictionary form أَعْلَام means standards; ships carried high on the sea are compared to them, making the raised-sign image visible.
The source-section root و س م includes reading a trace; this verse calls the ruins آيَات for الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ, those who discern marks.
The source-section dictionary form وَسْم is a brand; this verse threatens to place a visible brand, سَنَسِمُهُ, on a person's nose.
The section links height to recognizable marks; people on الْأَعْرَاف identify both groups by their سِيمَاهُم.
The source-section image is a mark by which a person is known; this verse says the needy are recognized by their سِيمَاهُم.
The source-section treats an outward mark as identifying; this verse says the Prophet would recognize hypocrites by their سِيمَاهُم.
The section's brand or sign identifies its bearer; this verse locates the believers' distinguishing mark on their faces, سِيمَاهُم.
The section's mark makes a person recognizable; this verse says criminals are known by their سِيمَاهُم.
The source-section dictionary form وَسْم is a trace one reads; this verse tells the reader to look at آثار رحمة الله in the revived earth.
The section says created kinds are marks by which one knows them; peoples and tribes are made لِتَعَارَفُوا, so their distinctions serve recognition.
The section presents creation's variety as identifying signs; this verse calls differences of tongues and colors among His signs, آيَاتِهِ.
The section joins a sign with height; Mary and her son are made آيَة and sheltered on رَبْوَةٍ, an elevated place.
The section says each created kind can be a sign; Mary and her son are explicitly made آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ.
The section reads the ark's movement under God's name; this verse makes Noah and the ark a sign for الْعَالَمِينَ.
The section names Noah's vessel; after the flood this verse says the ship was left as آيَة, a surviving trace to remember.
The section places Noah's vessel under God's name; this verse calls the loaded ship itself a sign, آيَةً لَهُمْ.
The source-section dictionary form الْعَالَمِينَ means the created world; Pharaoh asks who its Lord is, making the world's identity the question.
The section calls creation a field of signs that can be known; this verse names the heavens, earth, rain, winds, ships, and clouds as آيَات for people who reason.
The section treats creation as marks that disclose their maker; this verse calls the creation of heavens and earth and the night-day alternation signs for people of understanding.
The section links signs with knowing and invoking the named Lord; these readers remember Allah and call him رَبَّنَا after reflecting on creation.
The section's mark is for knowing; this verse makes stars landmarks for navigation and calls them signs for people who know.
The section says each kind of creation is a sign; this verse displays distinct crops, fruits, and growth as signs for people who believe.
The section says signs enable knowledge; the sun, moon, and their measured phases let people know years and reckoning.
The section joins a raised sign to what is known; this verse says the raised heavens and subjected sun and moon are signs for certainty about meeting their Lord.
The section says the created world is made of signs; this verse calls the ordered night, day, sun, moon, and stars signs for people who reason.
The section's الْعَالَمِين are created kinds, each a sign; this verse calls the varied colors of what is on earth a sign for people who heed.
The section treats each created kind as a sign; the bee's varied honey is called a sign for people who reflect.
The section's sign makes something knowable; night and day are two signs used to count years and reckoning.
The section's world is a field of signs; this verse calls the revived dead earth a sign and points to grain growing from it.
The section distinguishes a sign from what it identifies; sun, moon, night, and day are signs, yet the verse forbids worshipping them and directs worship to their Creator.
The section says created kinds distinguish and reveal; the creation of humans and scattered animals is explicitly called signs for people of certainty.
The source-section gloss says a good name spreads among people; this verse says, وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ, your mention was raised.
The source-section root س م و links the name to elevation; here the good word, الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ, ascends to God.
The source-section gloss describes a good name raised among people; this verse gives Abraham's family لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا, an elevated truthful mention.
The source-section says a good name travels among people; Abraham asks for لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ, a truthful mention among later generations.
The source-section describes good renown passing among people; Noah is left in later generations as a remembered name.
The section's good name spreads through generations; Abraham is left in later generations.
The section says a good mention continues among people; Moses and Aaron are left in later generations.
The section's good name is carried among people; Elijah is left in later generations.
The source-section root س م و means height and explains اسم as a raised identifier; this command joins اسم with الْأَعْلَى.
The source-section treats اسم as a raised, honored identifier; this verse blesses the Lord's name and names His majesty and generosity.
The source-section connects the name to elevation; the command is to glorify باسم ربك العظيم, the name of the Lord the Great.
The source-section links a name with honor; this repeated command again says to glorify باسم ربك العظيم.
The source-section's name-as-honored-sign meets the command to glorify باسم ربك العظيم.
The source-section says a name marks the beginning of an act; here reading begins بِاسْمِ the Lord who created.
The source-section dictionary form سَمِيّ means a counterpart deserving His name; this verse joins worship with the question whether He has any namesake or equal.
The source-section says names identify and call their bearer; this verse permits calling Allah or الرحمن and says the beautiful names belong to Him.
The source section notes resistance to the name الرحمن; here people ask who الرحمن is when told to prostrate to Him.
The source-section word اسم is an identifying mark; Joseph says the gods people worship are only names, أَسْمَاء, that they and their fathers invented.
The source-section's name identifies what it names; Hud challenges his people over names they and their fathers assigned to gods without authority.
The source-section says a name can be a sign with nothing true beneath it; this verse calls the idols names people and their fathers invented without God's authority.
The source-section says a name is what makes a thing known; Allah teaches Adam الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا.
This neighbor completes the naming scene: Adam is told to inform the angels of the names, making the taught names usable for recognition.
The source-section defines a name as what identifies a person; Mary's mother says سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ, I have named her Mary.
The source-section's names are identifying signs and calls; this verse says Allah has الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ and commands calling Him by them.
The source-section discusses Allah's names as ways to call and know Him; this verse says the most beautiful names belong to Allah alone.
The source-section treats names as signs by which the named is known; this verse lists Allah's names as Creator, Fashioner, and the possessor of الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ.
The source-section places worship under the known name; here God identifies Himself as Allah, then commands worship and remembrance.
The source-section's name identifies its bearer; this verse begins قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ, naming Allah as the One.
The source-section's سَمِيّ is an equal deserving the name; this verse denies that anyone is كُفُوًا, His counterpart.
The source-section says the name raises and identifies the named; this verse names the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, then calls him وَجِيهًا in this life and the next.
The source-section distinguishes a true identifying name from an empty label; this verse says adopted sons are not actual sons despite people's words.
The source-section says a name should identify its bearer; this verse commands calling adopted children by their fathers' names as more just with God.
The source-section's name at a letter's head identifies its sender; the queen first reports receiving a noble letter, setting up the identification in 27:30.
The source-section says بِسْمِ الله identifies whose name an act or message bears; this letter states it is from Solomon and begins in God's name.
The source-section says an act begins under a recognized name; Noah calls the passengers aboard بِسْمِ اللَّهِ and places the ark's motion and stopping under it.
The source-section dictionary form ع ل م is a distinguishing sign; Safa and Marwa are named as مِن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ, visible ritual markers traversed in pilgrimage.
The source-section says an act can be marked by Allah's name; pilgrims are told to mention His name over the livestock He provided.
The source-section's name identifies the giver and consecrates an act; every community is told to mention Allah's name over its provision of livestock.
The source-section links God's name to an action on an animal; here Allah's name is mentioned over sacrificial camels standing in rows.
The source-section says a name marks the beginning of an act; trained hunting animals are sent with Allah's name mentioned over the catch.
The source-section says naming identifies an act under Allah; this verse permits eating what has had Allah's name mentioned over it.
The section says a sign enables recognition; the new moons are appointed marks of time for people and pilgrimage.
The source-section links name, knowledge, and worship; this verse commands remembering the name of one's Lord and devoting oneself to Him.
The source-section treats the name as an invoked mark; this verse commands remembering the name of one's Lord morning and evening.
The source-section joins God's name with worship; this verse says the successful person remembers his Lord's name and prays.
The source-section links a name to elevation; this verse speaks of houses raised and Allah's name remembered within them.
The section contrasts Allah's known name with invented names; this verse says disbelievers recoil when Allah alone is mentioned but rejoice at other names.
This continuation explicitly calls the same ruined town a sign for believers, completing the sign-reading scene introduced at 15:75.
The section's good-name image is a sign that remains; this verse reverses it with an evil word like a tree uprooted without stability.
The section treats the name as a sign that identifies an act; this verse sets the outward meat and blood apart from the piety that reaches Allah.
The source-section puts an act under Allah's name; this verse draws the opposite boundary around food over which His name was not mentioned.
The section makes the name a sign that identifies allegiance; this verse condemns assigning rules to livestock whose meat was forbidden because Allah's name was not mentioned.
The source-section's بِسْمِ اللَّهِ marks an act under God; this verse forbids what was dedicated in the name of another.
The source-section marks an act with Allah's name; this verse excludes food over which another name was invoked.
The source-section places an act under Allah's name; this verse forbids an animal dedicated to someone other than Him.
The source-section's named beginning marks allegiance; this verse excludes what has been dedicated to other than Allah.
The source-section dictionary gloss of الْعَالَمِينَ includes the heavens and what they contain; this answer defines the worlds as the Lord of the heavens, earth, and between them.
The section presents each kind of creation as a marker; this verse distinguishes mountains, rivers, and gardens and calls them signs for people who reflect.
The section says one kind of creation is distinguished from another; this verse contrasts neighboring plots and date palms watered by the same water as signs for people who reason.
The section's sign is meant to guide recognition; this neighbor completes the landmarks with stars by which people find their way.
The section reads created kinds as marks; this verse describes the earth's paths and the water that brings out distinct plants.
The source-section says each created kind is a sign; this continuation points to diverse plants and livestock as signs for people of understanding.
The section says each created kind is itself a marker; this verse makes livestock a عِبْرَة, pointing to their milk and other benefits as a concrete created kind to recognize.
The section makes the created order readable; this verse calls the alternation of night and day a lesson for people with sight.
The section's sign makes a thing perceptible; this verse contrasts night for rest with a day made visible and calls it signs for believers.
The section says creation can be read as a mark; this verse calls the night a sign when daylight is drawn away.
The section treats created things as readable signs; this verse calls the revived, once-humbled earth one of God's signs.
The section says the worlds are signs by which the Lord becomes known; this verse promises signs in the horizons and within people until the truth is clear.
The section calls creation a collection of signs; this verse identifies signs in the heavens and earth for believers.
The section makes the created order readable; this verse names night and day, rain, and winds as signs for people who reason.
The section says creation is marked for recognition; this verse says there are signs on earth for those with certainty.
The source-section image extends signs to every created kind; this neighbor places signs within human selves as well.
The section's burned mark makes the bearer readable; here hearing, sight, and skins testify to what people did.
The source-section pictures a mark on skin; this continuation has the skins answer that Allah made them speak, exposing their owners' deeds.
The section uses an attached brand as an identifying mark; this verse pictures each person's deeds fastened to the neck and a record brought out on judgment day.
The source-section says a name is a raised sign and good mention spreads; this verse pictures a good word with firm roots and branches in the sky.
This neighbor completes Noah's preserved mention with the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ.
This neighbor supplies the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ that completes Abraham's lasting mention.
This neighbor supplies the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ, completing their continued mention.
This neighbor gives the public greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ, completing Elijah's continued mention.
The source-section dictionary form سَمِيّ appears here in its ordinary namesake sense for Yahya, distinct from the divine no-equal question at 19:65.
The source-section's name marks the actual identity of its bearer; this verse says a wife called a man's mother is not truly his mother.
This neighbor continues the sailing scene named in 11:41, showing the ark moving among waves like mountains.
This verse gives the ark scene that frames Noah's later words of praise and prayer when aboard in 23:28-29.
The source-section presents an action placed under God's name; Noah's passengers are told to praise Allah when settled aboard the ark.
The source-section has Noah name God over the ark's course and landing; here he prays, رَبِّ أَنْزِلْنِي, for a blessed landing.
The source-section connects invoking God to the start of a journey; this verse tells riders to remember their Lord when settled on a conveyance.
This neighbor gives the riding invocation, سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا, paralleling Noah's naming of the ark's motion.
The source section describes a raised sign that is recognized and honored; this verse says honoring شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ comes from piety of hearts.
This neighbor repeats the named-food rule while explaining its boundary and exception for necessity.
This neighbor shows the named houses in use: trade does not distract their people from remembrance, prayer, and giving.
The source-section says a name is raised and remembered; this verse condemns those who prevent Allah's name from being mentioned in His mosques.
The source-section makes the invoked name a sign that places the listener before God; here believers' hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned.
The source-section's opening joins Allah, الرحمن, and الرحيم; this verse names one God as Allah, the Most Merciful and Compassionate.
The source-section's reading begins by naming the Creator; this neighbor says the Lord taught by the pen, a tool that raises visible marks into knowledge.
This neighbor completes the pen image by saying God taught humanity what it did not know, linking a written sign to knowing.
The source-section dictionary example is a branded camel; this verse calls Salih's she-camel an آيَة from Allah, a distinct camel-sign without saying it is branded.
The source-section dictionary form uses a camel bearing a mark; this verse likewise identifies Allah's she-camel as a sign and sets a boundary around its use.
The source-section dictionary example is a branded camel; this verse calls Thamud's she-camel a visible sign, الناقة مبصرة, without claiming it bears a brand.
The section's trace-reading verse points back to a city turned upside down and pelted with stones; this ayah supplies the visible aftermath that 15:75 calls signs.
This continuation places the overturned town on a road that remains, making the aftermath in 15:74-75 a trace travelers can encounter.
This angelic reply says their descent is only by their Lord's command; that stance of acting under His authority sets up, but is distinct from, 19:65's worship and namesake question.
